subject: Privileged exec summary sanitization and phased report release
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <r.mehta@acme-security.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for pen test report and exec summary (NDA/redaction pref)

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team finished the intake and we'd like to review Redwood's most recent penetration test and the executive summary to validate residual risk for procurement. Specifically: 1) the full PT report (redaction acceptable) and 2) an exec summary suitable for our CISO and procurement.

We have an internal policy that requires a mutual NDA before full reports are exchanged. Can Redwood propose a redaction approach (what will be removed: hostnames, internal IPs, customer identifiers) and confirm whether you can provide a time‑bound, watermarked view for external reviewers? If you already have a standard mutual NDA we can sign, please send.

Ideal timing: we are trying to complete review by Oct 8 — would a phased delivery work (exec summary first, then redacted technical appendix)?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Security Lead, Acme Industries

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can absolutely support a phased delivery. Proposed next steps from our side:
- Share a sanitized exec summary to your CISO/procurement within 48 hours.
- Provide a redaction matrix + redacted report to a small set of named reviewers via timebound, watermarked DocSend link (or our secure viewer) 
- Full, unredacted report only on execution of a mutual NDA and a reviewer list/justification.

Looping in Karthik (security) for the technical redaction matrix and Marissa (legal) for NDA/DocuSign.

Camila

Date: 2026-09-27T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request for pen test report and exec summary (NDA/redaction pref)

Rajiv — quick technical note on redaction and delivery options so we align expectations: 

1) Typical redactions: internal hostnames, cloud provider instance IDs, internal IP ranges, customer‑specific identifiers, and any PII from test accounts. We do not remove vulnerability descriptions or risk ratings — the goal is to preserve remediation context.

2) Phased delivery I recommend:
  • Phase 1 (48–72h): Exec summary (one‑page risk overview) + annotated remediation tracker.
  • Phase 2 (within 1 week): Redacted report (redaction matrix attached) delivered via time‑bound DocSend or our secure viewer with watermark per user.
  • Phase 3 (on NDA + approved reviewer list): Full report delivery and technical Q&A session (30–60m) with our engineer.

3) Evidence snapshot: our PT vendor captures remediation evidence as of the scan date. If you need a follow‑up verification window, we can schedule a short re‑scan after fixes.

I attached a redaction matrix (redaction‑matrix.xlsx) showing fields we typically blank or obfuscate — let us know if Acme requires any deviations.

—Karthik
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redaction-matrix.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Mehta <r.mehta@acme-security.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request for pen test report and exec summary (NDA/redaction pref)

Rajiv / Camila — legal here. A few items from a contract perspective: 

• NDA: we can provide a mutual NDA with a limited‑purpose clause (review of security posture for procurement) and a 12‑month confidentiality period. Preferred: DocuSign link (I will send it when Camila confirms the reviewer list).
• IP carveouts: Redwood requests that vulnerability findings remain Redwood‑confidential and are not republished; standard non‑disclosure language will apply.
• Access controls: we require named reviewers and will enable watermarking and time limits (DocSend or our viewer). No mass circulation.

Attached is a sanitized exec summary (exec‑summary‑sanitized.docx) for initial review — we've redacted hostnames and internal IPs and included a high‑level remediation status table. If Acme needs additional masking (e.g., merging certain findings), flag those items with line refs.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-29T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Phased release plan and next steps — Acme pen test materials

Hi Rajiv / Alicia — thanks for the quick responses. Per our internal review, here is the phased release plan we propose: 

Phase 1 (today): share exec summary (attached) and remediation tracker for procurement/CISO review. Watermarked, downloadable as PDF for named recipients.
Phase 2 (by 2026-10-04): provide redacted technical appendix via DocSend (timebound links, unique viewer per reviewer). See attached redaction matrix for specifics.
Phase 3 (on mutual NDA + approved reviewer list): deliver the full report and schedule a 45‑minute technical Q&A with Karthik. If you confirm reviewers and sign the NDA, we can release Phase 3 by 2026‑10‑08.

Action items for Acme: 
  1) Confirm the small reviewer list (name + role + email) — reply to this thread.
  2) Approve mutual NDA — we will send DocuSign once reviewers are confirmed.
  3) Confirm whether DocSend or our secure viewer is preferred for Phase 2 (we recommend DocSend since it is already configured for watermarks).

DocSend link (Phase 1 materials — exec summary): https://docsend.com/view/acme-pt
Drive link (redaction matrix): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcDEF

If that timeline works I will send the DocuSign NDA and enable the Phase 2 links.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
